alignments.note: Rule 83: reciprocal heads on the allos-word another, not the supplied one.
Anarthrous noun takes its supplied determiner as a rule 7/51 helper.
Rule 17: a source noun rendered of + noun heads on the noun.

Verbless clause with an expressed lexical noun subject, so rule 63's exception (which is the subject PRONOUN's alone) does not reach it and the supplied copula is the predicate's helper, even against the ASV's word order; the dative predicate takes 'be' with its case preposition 'unto' riding along under rule 21, no Greek preposition being expressed for rule 36 to govern. Rule 62 answers the objection that rule 53 names only prepositional, adjectival and adverbial predicates: the test does not turn on the verb being a copula, and an expressed subject does not change it. 2PE.3.18 is the unhedged twin.

Rule 31: the article's modifier is a prepositional phrase, so the article keeps the supplied relativizer and the copula goes with the preposition. The quantifier pasin has already taken 'all', so only 'that' is left to the article, as EPH.2.17's tois -> 'that' has only the relativizer where hymin supplies the pronoun.
Rules 31 and 53: a prepositional phrase has no verb to carry the supplied copula, so are in belongs to en.
